Practice_Description: Judima is reported in community celebrations including Bushu and hospitality settings.

Occasion_or_Context: Hospitality, agricultural work and social/ritual occasions
Practice_Description: Research describes Apong as a social beverage offered to guests and associated with agricultural life; some accounts describe use in ritual and community events.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Published research; exact practices differ by source
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not assume all events, customary rules or forms are shared across every Mising village or household.

Practice_Description: A 2007 ethnobotanical study reports Sujen at festivals and celebrations and in some birth and marriage ceremonies; it also describes earlier hospitality customs. Other studies describe it as culturally important. Attribute these accounts to their source and period.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Deori, Begum and Mao (2007); later ethnobotanical surveys
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: The 2007 fieldwork was conducted in 2003–2004; these descriptions do not prove identical current practice in all Deori villages.

Occasion_or_Context: Marriage, worship, festivals, hospitality and social occasions
Practice_Description: Teron (2006) reports Hor-alank in traditional marriage and worship contexts and Hor-arak at social occasions, including death ceremonies and guest hospitality. The Government of West Karbi Anglong page also describes Hor and Horpo in Karbi rituals and events. Keep the forms and contexts distinct and attribute claims to their sources.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Teron (2006); Government of West Karbi Anglong district website
Evidence_Type: Historical field research and government cultural overview
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not assume the same form is used at every ceremony or that the same customs apply across all Karbi localities today.

State: Assam; related research locality in West Bengal
District: Goalpara (Assam); Rasikbill Rabha basti, Cooch Behar (West Bengal)
Practice_Description: Research describes Jonga-mod/Choko as a traditional rice-based beverage with a role in Rabha household and community life. A 2023 study notes that Chokot contributes to dietary intake in its studied community and documents women involved in starter preparation. Broader ceremony-specific claims need source- and locality-specific evidence.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Deka and Sarma (2010); Bhuyan and Baishya (2013); Bhattacharjee et al. (2023)
Evidence_Type: Ethnobotanical field research, review and laboratory study
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not infer identical customs across Rabha communities in Assam and North Bengal or treat reported medicinal uses as clinically established.

District: Sivasagar and broader Upper Brahmaputra Valley; exact ritual locality needs verification
Practice_Description: Reviews associate Xaj with Tai-Ahom social and religious life and mention Bihu. Duarah, Kalita and Mishra (2023) report starter preparation around Rongali and Bhogali Bihu and a community function called Haaj’r hokam. Keep these details attributed to those sources until corroborated by community-led, locality-specific accounts.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Frontiers in Microbiology (2022) review; Duarah, Kalita and Mishra (2023) survey/review
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not assume every Tai-Ahom household follows the same calendar or ritual use; confirm terminology, current practice and what knowledge is public with community sources.

Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Verify details by product and locality.

Practice_Description: The reviewed sources describe Zu/Chu as part of Tiwa community life; exact ceremony-specific contexts need confirmation from the full study and community-approved sources.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Goswami et al. (2020); Duarah et al. (2023)
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not convert traditional medicinal claims into clinical claims; avoid asserting a universal ceremonial role without locality-specific evidence.

Practice_Description: A 2026 account describes Haria as a traditional beverage embedded in Tea-tribe community life and says consumption is especially prominent during summer. More specific ritual, life-cycle, or village-level practices require corroboration.

Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Do not generalize this seasonal pattern or assign ritual uses to every Tea-tribe community; reported cultural context is not evidence of medical efficacy.

District: Southern Assam study region; exact sample village not reported
Occasion_or_Context: Ritual, religious, social, and special-occasion contexts reported in ethnographic literature
Practice_Description: A 2020 ethnographic account describes Zou in contexts including rituals, hearings, feasts, festivals and marital negotiations. It describes Nduizou/herazou as a sacred drink used on special occasions. A 2016 article analyses the role of zao in debates around religion and culture among Zeme Nagas.
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Practices are not necessarily universal or unchanged; do not infer that all Zeme households use the beverage in the same ways, and respect religious diversity and community preferences.

District: Southern Assam study region; exact sample villages unresolved
Occasion_or_Context: Social, ritual and community contexts reported at a broad level
Practice_Description: The 2026 southern Assam study reports that traditional rice beverages have distinct ritual, social and medicinal functions within each studied community, including Hmar. A Mizoram government account refers to Zu in a Chapchar Kut origin narrative; it is contextual evidence for regional Mizo festival history, not proof of the same practice in every Assam Hmar community.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Yumnam, Nath & Sharma (2026); Directorate of Information & Public Relations, Government of Mizoram
Evidence_Type: Peer-reviewed field study and official cultural narrative
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Keep Assam-specific claims separate from Mizoram narratives; reported medicinal uses are ethnographic beliefs, not clinical evidence.

Occasion_or_Context: Festivals, sacrificial rituals, deity offerings, ceremonies and everyday social consumption
Practice_Description: The 2023 participatory study reports Rohi in festivals and traditional sacrificial ceremonies, as an offering to deities before consumption, and in everyday social life. It describes the fermentation technology as knowledge held by women in its study context.
Reported_by_Source_or_Community: Ripunjoy Sonowal (2023), based on interviews, discussions and observation
Evidence_Type: Participatory ethnographic and technical field study
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Study-specific findings; do not universalize across every Sonowal Kachari household or village. Respect knowledge holders and gendered knowledge traditions.

Occasion_or_Context: Social functions and regular consumption reported for Rohi and Sepa collectively
Practice_Description: The 2026 article states that Rohi and Sepa are regularly consumed and important in Sonowal Kachari social functions, but does not specify which functions are associated with Sepa alone in its abstract.
Cautions_or_Qualifiers: Collective claim for both beverages; Sepa-specific ritual or occasion details remain unverified.
